checkpoint: ROADMAP ITEM 4 §5 — pure lifecycle kernel fixtures
scopeLimit: The kernel is pure. These fixtures prove its legal vocabulary, conjunctive stabilization gate, action bounds, event-bounded living condition and ownership table. The world-level stabilization audit proves the production adapter.

fixtures.claim: every phase declares a coherent temporal, event-bounded or terminal resolution kind, and no quantity is owned twice
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: the complete production phase table is present

fixtures.claim: the kernel admits stabilization only behind the complete named proof
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: the pure kernel exercised the reserved legal path; this is not a production-writer claim

fixtures.claim: a provisional successor opens in travelling, never in establishing
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: establishing exists as a phase, so opening in travelling is a choice rather than an absence

fixtures.claim: an attempt can be abandoned from every pre-departure phase
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: all three pre-departure phases were exercised

fixtures.claim: departure is refused without a founder count the residual authority endorsed
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: a valid endorsed count DOES depart, so the refusals are refusals and not an inert gate

fixtures.claim: all four stabilization claims are independently required, while an establishment timeout is a failure
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: the complete conjunction succeeds, so each named refusal isolates a missing claim

fixtures.claim: every action resolves at its temporal bound while a living condition refuses timeout authority
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: every timed action crossed its bound and every event-bounded living phase received a timeout attempt

fixtures.claim: no transition leaves a terminal phase
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: every terminal phase in the production table was exercised against every possible destination

fixtures.claim: every transition outside the permitted set is refused
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: both permitted and refused transitions genuinely occur in the sweep

fixtures.claim: early failure leads only to returning — never to stabilization, never to a stop
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: the phase's exits are enumerated from the production table and none of them is a success

fixtures.claim: no phase lets the parent and the successor own the same quantity
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: both sides of the departure are represented in the table

fixtures.claim: lifecycle history cannot grow without bound
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: the drive genuinely exceeded the cap

fixtures.claim: the same request produces a byte-identical result
information the kernel has no field for cannot alter a transition
fixtures.nonVacuityNote: unrelated keys were genuinely present on the request
